Read the following fictional engineering brief.

1. The team is comparing three local inference engines on the same battery-powered device. Engine Cedar opens a compact model quickly but decodes slowly, engine Juniper spends longer preparing its model but has steadier generation, and engine Rowan uses more memory in exchange for faster prompt processing. All measurements must distinguish setup, prompt processing, and token generation.

2. The application normally remains open for twenty to forty minutes, although some users close it immediately after one request. A route with expensive setup can therefore be reasonable only when the loaded session is reused. The recommendation should account for both a one-request visit and a longer session without combining their timing boundaries.

3. The device has limited memory and the operating system may reclaim background processes under pressure. Mapped model files, private anonymous allocations, shared pages, runtime workspaces, and the growing key-value cache do not have identical memory semantics. Peak sampled proportional set size and process high-water marks must be labeled rather than treated as interchangeable.

4. Prompt lengths vary substantially. A short request contains only a direct instruction, a medium request includes several pages of notes, and a long request approaches the useful context expected by the application. Token counts differ across model tokenizers even when the exact UTF-8 prompt bytes are identical.

5. Time to first token includes work a user experiences before text appears, while prefill throughput isolates processing of the input tokens. Decode throughput describes the later stream of generated tokens. A runtime that exposes only one combined timing cannot be credited with an invented split between prefill and sampling.

6. The first request can trigger page faults, lazy runtime initialization, cache allocation, or accelerator compilation that later requests avoid. Repeated requests must clear conversation and key-value state while retaining the loaded model session. The report must preserve the first observation separately from the same-session distribution.

7. Thermal conditions are not constant. Sustained generation may heat the phone enough to change clock rates, and charging can change both power and temperature. The operator records the battery and thermal state before and after the campaign and does not describe an unmeasured power value as zero.

8. Outputs are retained so that obvious execution failures remain visible. A nonempty string is not automatically useful: a broken route may emit token identifiers, binary-looking fragments, repeated punctuation, or a short loop. The initial screen asks only whether the exact output looks like sensible text and deliberately avoids a broader quality claim.

9. The candidate artifacts come from different sources. Some are original floating-point checkpoints, some are community conversions, and some are quantized packages produced by a separate toolchain. A model label alone is insufficient provenance; source revision, file hashes, format, quantization method, and conversion tool must remain attached to every route.

10. Tokenizer and chat-template behavior can change independently of the model weights. The benchmark therefore records tokenizer revision, template provenance, the final rendered-prompt hash, the effective token count, and a hash of token identifiers. It never forces one model family's tokenizer onto another family merely to obtain matching token counts.

11. The application needs a transcript-capable generation ceiling, but the ceiling is not an instruction to produce exactly that many tokens. A model may stop at its end-of-sequence token, match an explicit stop sequence, reach the ceiling, time out, or fail. The actual generated count and stop reason are part of every run.

12. One engine reports accelerator assignment at session creation but silently falls back during unsupported operations. Another performs preprocessing on the CPU while all neural layers use the accelerator. Provider claims must identify what executed where, and a host compatibility run cannot substitute for physical-device evidence.

13. The test device is shared with normal development work. Background downloads, another benchmark process, or a stale remote directory can invalidate resource observations. The campaign uses an exclusive device lock, records relevant concurrent activity, and cleans only paths owned by the current experiment.

14. Model setup has a declared readiness boundary. It begins before the first model or tokenizer file is opened or the runtime is created, whichever occurs first, and ends only when a request can be accepted without additional model loading, session creation, accelerator compilation, or initial cache allocation. Offline conversion remains a separately reported preparation cost.

15. A runtime may stream byte fragments that do not yet form visible characters. The benchmark timing uses delivery of the first generated token identifier to the caller, while the retained raw output contains the final decoded UTF-8 text. If the runtime cannot expose token delivery precisely, the limitation and substitute callback boundary are recorded.

16. Decode throughput excludes the already measured prompt tokens. It uses the number of generated tokens represented by the timed decode interval and states whether the first generated token is included. A single headline token rate without its numerator, denominator, and tokenizer identity is not sufficient evidence.

17. The team expects measurements to be regenerated later on a different Android release. Device model, system build, ABI, runtime libraries, thread count, provider options, and model package must therefore be explicit. A later refresh is added as new dated evidence instead of overwriting the original run.

18. Some models cannot fit the long workload plus the output ceiling in their declared context window. Such a route must fail or mark that tier unavailable with a reason. Silently truncating the prompt, reducing the ceiling, or dropping the system message would create a different workload and invalidate a matched comparison.

19. Memory sampling can miss a short-lived peak, whereas a cumulative high-water mark can include allocations from earlier phases. Both observations can be useful when their methods and lifecycles are preserved. Neither should be relabeled as isolated model memory, accelerator memory, or key-value-cache size without direct evidence.

20. The registry is an index over committed experiment evidence rather than a replacement for it. Raw per-request records stay with the experiment, while normalized rows expose route identity, workload, aggregate measurements, limitations, and evidence paths. Missing values remain null with a concrete reason.

21. The team will evaluate transcript quality in a later phase. The current performance campaign does not score narrative structure, factual accuracy, style, pacing, grounding, or editing burden. A text that passes the superficial sanity screen has demonstrated only that the route did not obviously collapse on those exact output bytes.

22. Different prompt tiers can have different effective token counts and prefill costs. Results are grouped by exact tier and are not pooled into one rate. Distributions with different repetition contracts are not presented as matched, even when their medians happen to be numerically close.

23. Timeout handling is fail-closed. The operator retains partial text and available timing when possible, identifies the timeout as the stop reason, and leaves measurements that never occurred unavailable. A timeout does not become a zero-token-per-second result unless the underlying numerator and interval actually establish that value.

24. The benchmark uses greedy decoding for the first comparable performance contract. This reduces sampling variance, but byte-identical output is still not a required pass condition because kernels, runtimes, and numerical paths can diverge. Any observed variation is retained and described rather than filtered out.

25. Long-running phone measurements can be distorted by screen state, charging state, radio activity, and operating-system scheduling. The runner records the controlled conditions it can establish and lists the rest as limitations. Operational discipline is part of the evidence, not a guarantee that every uncontrolled variable disappeared.

26. A useful report separates what the route proved from why the team might choose it. Fast decoding may not compensate for excessive setup in short sessions, and a low-memory route may still be impractical if prompt processing is too slow. The final recommendation should describe these tradeoffs without inventing product requirements.

27. The comparison also distinguishes artifact storage from runtime memory. Package bytes affect installation and download cost, mapped pages affect process accounting, and runtime caches grow with context and output. Reporting only the model file size would not answer whether the route fits comfortably on the phone.

28. Each raw output is small enough to commit as text, unlike model weights and large binary profiles. Its file path, byte count, and SHA-256 bind later observations to exact bytes. If someone checks output sanity later, the registry can add that exact-hash observation without changing the original performance measurements.

29. The benchmark should remain usable across CPU, GPU, and NPU routes. It therefore defines external timing and evidence boundaries without choosing an accelerator in advance. Provider-specific proof belongs to the experiment and must support, rather than replace, the common setup and request measurements.

30. The immediate decision is which routes deserve deeper deployment work. The evidence should make blocked and negative results useful by preserving where they stopped, which tiers ran, and what remained unavailable. It should not turn a successful smoke test into a production-readiness claim.

Write a self-contained technical recommendation for the team. Explain the important tradeoffs, identify the measurements that should remain separate, and end with a practical next step. Use ordinary prose rather than a table.<|im_end|>
